title: Remove a bolt whose backed-out head has trapped the ratchet against a bulkhead
justification: Candidate automotive-service manipulation: a fastener has been backed out without accounting for axial tool clearance. Occupation size and frequency of this exact recovery still require evidence; do not treat the category bar as established.
fault: The socket remains engaged on a partly withdrawn bolt, with the ratchet head nearly touching a rigid bulkhead behind it. Further loosening reduces clearance and prevents straight tool withdrawal.
instruction: Remove the mounting bolt and leave it with the socket and ratchet on the bench.
objects: Full-scale mounting bracket with threaded bolt and nut or threaded boss
Rigid adjacent bulkhead that constrains axial tool clearance
Correctly sized socket with real engagement cavity
Reversible ratchet with direction selector and square drive
Two or three SimReady workshop distractors outside the tool path
skill: Recognize an axial-clearance dead end; reverse enough threaded travel to recover withdrawal space, disengage the drive, then complete removal using a physically feasible alternative grip. Tool geometry, thread pitch and clearances must support the entire sequence.
scoring: Draft, not implemented: 0.5 for extracting and releasing an intact bolt outside its threaded boss; 1.0 additionally requires the ratchet and socket disengaged and all three parts resting on the bench with grippers at least 3 cm clear for 3 s. Any broken fixture, stripped thread or part leaving the bench gives 0. All other outcomes give 0. Numeric geometry and damage thresholds must be established from real hardware before building.

nearest.title: Fasten a bracket bolt with a ratchet in confined access
Undo a tight bolt with a ratchet that is set to tighten: check its direction lever, flip it, then swing it

risks: Strict-review objection: recovery direction may only change the starting layout of accepted PR 890; a fault label does not establish novelty.
A discrete selector puzzle plus ordinary ratcheting may fail the physical-difficulty bar.
No evidence yet that this exact recovery is core regular work rather than incidental tool management.

SimReady visual assets exist, but realistic hollow sockets, threaded travel, selector behavior and tool disengagement must be verified; a welded prop or proximity-triggered fake thread is insufficient.
A valid full-score route must remain possible after freeing the tool; cannot invent finger-loose torque or an extra tool to rescue a flawed scene.

review.decision: abandoned; do not build or submit
review.evidence: Live PR 890 is accepted. Live PR 1470 was finally rejected as a duplicate: reversing a socket ratchet and flipping its lever did not establish a distinct core physical skill. Axial trapping adds geometry but the present concept does not establish sufficient separation. The live board redirected to sign-in; novelty evidence here comes from the refreshed public GitHub index and PR reviews, not an authenticated board inspection.

tests.novelty: fails conservative internal screening: no convincing distinction from accepted confined-access ratcheting

review.validation: Concept review only. No task folder, simulator trials, demo scores, red-team scores, Dream run, upload or PR.
